resolutions: Directional on and huāl remain inside the VNC while antecessive and negative particles remain outside it.
Directional position is derived from Valence and object structure rather than selected as a separate spelling choice.
The rare on plus itt-a contraction remains an optional grammatical operation rather than a general spelling rule.
Antecessive ō is optional only where compatible past grammar licenses it and does not alter internal object spelling.
Negative ah takes scope outside the VNC and precedes antecessive ō when both occur.
Negative ca follows the negative scope rule but remains limited to its licensed trigger environments.
Statement, question, and exclamation are sentence uses; technical transformation classes are not user controls.
Positive, negative, and emphatic statements have distinct operations instead of being mislabeled as questions.
A yes-no question may be marked by intonation alone or by cuix, but both use question punctuation.
Cuix contributes question force while the verbstem and context retain responsibility for lexical interpretations.
